text:
Alex Ovechkin's final season isn't going the way anyone pictured. TSN noted he is goalless in 11 straight and on pace for about five goals, a strange number next to the greatest goal scorer the sport has seen. He did tie another franchise record in a win over Ottawa, but the goal light hasn't come.

The Capitals have spent the rest of the week answering for hits. Jakob Chychrun's hit put Nick Cousins out for 7 to 10 days and set off a public fallout, and Tom Wilson avoided a suspension for his hit on Florida's Sandis Vilmanis, a ruling Panthers writers didn't love. Wilson has one point in his last ten games on chances that usually produce five or six.

Washington is 10-8-0 with 20 points and the process sits in the middle: 53% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), but a penalty kill allowing 0.85 expected goals a game. Charlie Lindgren is at .851 and 3.8 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, and Logan Thompson was burned in a 7-4 loss to New Jersey as the Devils swept the home-and-home. Our playoff odds sit at 48%.

The bright spot is young. Ryan Leonard's line with Boone Jenner and Justin Sourdif has taken 73% of the chances in a small sample. What we'd watch: Ovechkin's next goal, because every one of them is now part of a farewell.
